case_type_reason: Onset is printed in weeks or months and findings are narrative; the measurements themselves are restricted medical data.
title: Seven ISS astronauts with vision changes (now SANS) from NASA's 2012 evidence report

input_data.use: Whether and when each crewman reported a vision change in flight

documented_outcome.quote: After exposure to spaceflight of 5 to 6 months duration, seven astronauts were discovered to have neuro-ophthalmic findings.
Lumbar punctures performed in four astronauts with disc edema showed opening pressures of 22, 21, 28, and 28.5 cm H2O performed at 60, 19, 12 and 57 days post-mission, respectively.

Three weeks after the ultrasound examination and Amlser grid testing, reading glasses (2.5 D and 3.25 D) were delivered to the ISS via a Shuttle mission and one astronaut reported that the 3.25 D glasses worked best.
the CO2 levels on the ISS are nominally between 2.3 to 5.3 mm Hg
documented_outcome.location: PDF page 20 (case 7; case 4 on PDF page 13 says CO2 was within normal operating levels)

onset_relative_to_data: In-flight onset of the reported vision change: case 5 after 3 weeks, cases 4 and 7 about 2 months, case 2 about 3 months, case 1 throughout the mission. Cases 3 and 6 reported nothing in flight; their findings came after return.

expected_product_output.rule_in_environment_hazards_json: Any new change in vision. A specialist eye examination is needed; threshold to be set by clinical review for what counts as a change.
expected_product_output.when: At the first daily check where the crewman logs the vision change

expected_product_output.role: The candidate the product names, with its 'needs specialist eye examination' answer; never a diagnosis.

expected_product_output.negative_control: Cases 3 and 6: no in-flight symptom, so no in-flight alert is expected. The product must not claim it would have caught them; only scheduled eye imaging could.

expected_product_output.context: CO2 was within normal ISS levels in the cases where the report states it, so a CO2 warning is not expected to co-occur.

consumers.use: Spare reading glasses in the plan

is_not: Not individual measurements; the report's Table 1 (an image) and the underlying OCT, fundus, MRI and IOP data were not used. Detailed astronaut medical data are released only through LSAH (see ../restricted-and-not-found.json).

viip2012.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Intracranial Hypertension and Vision Alterations (Risk of Microgravity-Induced Visual Impairment/Intracranial Pressure), Version 1.0, approved for public release 12 July 2012, Alexander, Gibson, Hamilton et al., NASA Human Research Program
